name: Social and Cultural Construction of Emotions
description: This course introduces theory and research on emotions, with a focus on the social and cultural underpinnings of mental processes that guide emotion appraisal, regulation, and expression. You will be directly exposed to major theoretical debates and empirical developments in the study of emotions. Lectures and discussions will range across multiple levels of analysis, from individual and interpersonal to social and cultural. You will learn about the general aspects of emotions as well as the role of specific emotions that play an important role in intergroup relations, such as anger, contempt, guilt, shame, humiliation, and disgust. Overall, this course brings together insights into emotions from the intersections of social, political, and cultural/cross-cultural psychology.
